subject: Post-discovery: plan dedicated sizing session & sample workload
body:
From: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@novapay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novapay.com>
Date: Sun, May 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Thanks for the discovery — next step: sizing call

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the rundown earlier — helpful for our stakeholders. We got alignment internally: we want a dedicated capacity sizing session focused on our fraud-detection inference workload (mostly short prompts, 8–32 tokens of context, high QPS bursts).

Two asks before we lock a time:
- Can you confirm what information you need from us (samples, qps patterns, latency SLOs)?
- Suggested windows for a 45–60 minute sizing call next week (we're Pacific time).

I've attached a sample extract of production requests and a very high-level infra diagram. Let me know if you need a larger sample set.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering | NovaPay
Attachment: novapay-workload-sample.csv (csv, 35 KB)
Attachment: high-level-arch-diagram.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)

-----
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@novapay.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novapay.com>
Date: Sun, May 30, 2027 at 10:03 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the discovery — next step: sizing call

Samantha — really appreciate the sample and the quick recap. High-level read looks good; that CSV will help us model the request distribution.

For the sizing call, our typical pre-call checklist is:
- Confirm representative workload (you sent a good start; if possible include peak-minute QPS and typical prompt length distribution).
- Clarify latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 targets) and acceptable tail-degradation during bursts.
- Any data residency or networking constraints (VPC egress, static IPs).
- Attendees: please include the person who owns infra and the decision-maker for procurement if possible.

We can do 45 minutes. Proposed time slots (PT):
- Tue, Jun 1 — 9:30–10:15am PT
- Tue, Jun 1 — 2:00–2:45pm PT
- Wed, Jun 2 — 11:00–11:45am PT

Mina (solutions eng) and Marcus (inference PM) will join to walk throughput/latency tradeoffs and mapping to Dedicated pool options.

If none of those work, send two windows that do and we'll prioritize. I'll also drop a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novapay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@novapay.com>
Date: Mon, May 31, 2027 at 08:18 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the discovery — next step: sizing call

Logan,

Thanks — Tue Jun 1 at 2:00pm PT works best for our team. I've looped in procurement (procurement@novapay.com) — they may ask for an estimated cost ballpark before the call so they can prep internal approvals.

Quick answers to your checklist:
- Peak-minute QPS (approx): 1,200–1,800 (bursts lasting 2–5 minutes).
- Typical prompt length: mean 24 tokens, 90th percentile 56 tokens.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms. Slightly flexible on p99 during 2–5 minute bursts if we can maintain p95.
- Data residency: must remain in us-west-2 region; we require VPC peering and static egress IPs for allowlists.

Attendees on our side: Samantha (platform), Alex (technical), Priya R. (security) — Priya will only dial in if we need to go deeper on VPC/KMS.

We uploaded a slightly larger workload sample to the Drive link Logan included.

Best,
Alex
Senior Engineering Manager | NovaPay

Attachment: novapay-workload-sample-expanded.csv (csv, 1.2 MB)

-----
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <s.ortiz@novapay.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novapay.com>, procurement@novapay.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, May 31, 2027 at 15:28 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the discovery — next step: sizing call

Perfect — locking Tue, Jun 1 2:00–2:45pm PT. Calendar invite sent (includes Zoom link and agenda).

Pre-call ask from our side (to speed the sizing exercise):
1) If possible, paste a 10-minute sample with timestamps showing the busiest minute (we use that to model KV cache hit rates).
2) Confirm a rough target throughput for sustained steady-state vs peak burst. You already gave ranges; if you can pick one steady-state target (e.g., 400 qps sustained) that helps our pool-sizing calc.
3) Any SLA must-have (e.g., p95 <= 250ms non-negotiable) — we'll treat that as a hard constraint when sizing.

We'll prepare two sizing scenarios in the call:
- Conservative: higher headroom for bursts (reduces chance of degraded p95)
- Cost-optimized: tighter steady-state with acceptable tail increases during short bursts

Mina and Marcus will share a short model (token-by-token cost and expected latency curves) and a recommended Dedicated pool configuration and autoscale strategy. Marcus will also bring a sample rollout plan to pin model versions and failover policies.

If procurement wants an early ballpark, our rough estimate range for an initial Dedicated pool to cover ~1,600 peak qps bursts with p95 <= 250ms would be included in the call materials. We can provide a written estimate after the session.

See you Tue.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
